I will start from what I did last year and only change a little. On my 10.1 mu, I will keep most land in the wheat-maize cycle because that is the steady way here, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton. Around here, if wheat and maize fertilizer is cut too hard, the field shows it fast, and I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose grain. I have well water, so I will use that to keep wheat safe at key times and help maize if summer rain is short. I did middle school, so I do look at seed and fertilizer a bit more carefully now than before. For wheat I will use an improved variety, put enough nitrogen for tillering and grain filling, and give 3 irrigations if the year is normal. For maize I will use hybrid seed like most people around me, keep fertilizer a bit stronger because maize eats fertilizer, and I will not be stingy at jointing and filling. For cotton I will keep a smaller area because it takes more watching and more spraying, but I will still plant some since I know how to manage it and it can bring cash if the year goes smoothly. I will balance spending across the whole farm, so I will not chase very high input, but I will not go low either.
